claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me. I'm wondering if I can still claim Child Benefit for him now that he's that age?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Yes, you may still be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex now that he's 16, but it depends on his circumstances.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, is he:
- Still in school or college?
- On an apprenticeship?
- In another form of approved training?

Or has he left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's finished school now - he left education. But I'm not entirely sure what his plans are yet. He might be looking at doing some kind of training or apprenticeship, but nothing's been sorted out yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex has left education, there are a few more details I need to understand his situation:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or with the armed services?** 

This is important because if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with one of these services, you can continue to get Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces yet. He's just been at home since leaving school, trying to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me also ask:

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now. He's just been at home since he finished school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I have a few more questions to make sure I understand your full situation:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. One final question to complete my assessment:

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or are you looking to make a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm looking to make a new claim - I haven't been claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time**.

Here's why:

For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can only continue if the child is under 20 **and** stays in approved education or training. Since Alex has left school and is not currently in any approved education or training, he doesn't meet this requirement.

There is also a special provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. However, Alex hasn't registered with either of these yet.

**What you could consider:**
- If Alex decides to return to education or approved training in the future, you could claim Child Benefit at that point
- If Alex registers with a government-sponsored careers service while looking for work or training, you may be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks during that period

I hope this helps clarify your situation. If Alex's circumstances change, it would be worth reconsidering your eligibility at that time.
